narrative.overview:
Unglish uses the familiar materials of Craigslist and late-1990s HTML: a plain page, system serif text, underlined links and native browser controls. The humour belongs in the writing. CSS provides legibility, responsive flow and accessible interaction.

The rendered site is a document with useful controls. Its browser conventions are intentional, including native disclosure markers and platform-dependent button and field appearance. The rejected polished print-reference-book direction is not part of this system.
keyCharacteristics: Left-aligned text, visible links and simple dividing rules.
System serif typography, including inherited text in controls.
Native controls and disclosures with clear keyboard focus.
Light and dark palettes with the same reading order.

rules.name: The Visible Link Rule
rules.body: Keep links underlined; increase underline thickness on hover and retain the visited colour.

rules.name: The Browser Serif Rule
rules.body: Preserve the system serif and native heading hierarchy; do not substitute a custom display face.

dos: **Do** use semantic headings, links, lists, fieldsets and disclosures.
**Do** retain native controls, including their browser-specific states.
**Do** preserve visible keyboard focus and allow controls and text to wrap.
**Do** use the matching light or dark palette across text, links and rules.
donts: **Don't** introduce cards, custom fonts, illustrated paper or decorative motion.
**Don't** replace underlined navigation links with decorative controls.
**Don't** turn the native-web document into a polished print-reference-book layout.
